questions.question: Differentiate between mass and weight.
questions.solution:
**Mass:**
- The quantity of matter contained in a body; it is a **scalar** and a **fundamental quantity**.
- Measured in kilograms (kg); SI base unit of mass.
- It is **independent** of location, gravitational field and the state of motion.
- It is **invariant** everywhere in the universe.
- Invariant mass is given by $m_0 = \dfrac{m_{rel}}{\gamma}$.

**Weight:**
- The force with which the earth attracts a body; $W = mg$.
- It is a **vector** (directed towards the centre of the earth) and a **derived quantity**.
- Measured in newtons (N) or kilogram-force; SI unit is the newton.
- It **varies** with $g$, so it changes with latitude, altitude and the celestial body.
- On the moon, weight is one-sixth of that on the earth while mass is unchanged.

**Apparent weight** $W_{app} = mg - F_{centrifugal}$ can even be zero during free fall.
questions.knowledgeNote: Mass is invariant scalar matter measured in kg; weight is the gravitational force mg measured in newton and varies with g.
